review_notes: I read the whole file, the BFEquiv simp lemmas in BackAndForth/Equivalence.lean, and the only downstream use (Scott/Sentence.lean). scottFormula_zero as simp is sound. Leaving scottFormula_add_one and scottFormula_limit non-simp is sensible, because they expand the definition and the limit lemma has hypotheses. The one questionable point is the simp attribute on the conditional iff lemma. This is low-to-moderate confidence: I did not run Lean, so I make no claim about observed simp behaviour. I found no cycle, and no competing rule inside this file.

findings.excerpt:
theorem realize_scottFormula_iff_bfEquiv [L.IsRelational] {N : Type w'} [L.Structure N]
    (a : Fin n → M) (b : Fin n → N) {α : Ordinal.{o}} (hα : α < ω₁) :
findings.problem: The lemma is tagged @[simp] but is conditional on `hα : α < ω₁`, which simp can only discharge when α is a concrete or already-hypothesized ordinal. Its right-hand side `BFEquiv α n a b` is also the left-hand side of the simp lemmas `BFEquiv.add_one` and `BFEquiv.limit`, so the attribute pulls simp into the BFEquiv expansion rules. Its only use, in `realize_scottSentenceAt`, passes it explicitly with `simp only [... realize_scottFormula_iff_bfEquiv _ _ hα, ...]`. The attribute therefore adds no benefit there. The simp set also lacks a corresponding rule for `scottFormula a (α+1)`, so the interface is asymmetric: `scottFormula_zero` is simp, but successor and limit are not.
findings.proposed_change: Drop `@[simp]` from `realize_scottFormula_iff_bfEquiv` and keep it as an explicitly supplied rewrite, as `Sentence.lean` already does. Alternatively, keep it only if there is a use that needs side-condition discharge by simp. If so, state the bound as an instance-like or simp-dischargeable hypothesis, and document which concrete ordinals it is meant for.
findings.benefit: This keeps the default simp set free of a conditional rewrite that rarely fires. It also stops that rewrite from chaining into `BFEquiv.add_one` and `BFEquiv.limit`, and it makes the intended explicit-argument usage clear.
